concept: Backup and PIT oplog storage region billing

claims.text: The primary backup region and each additional copy region receive their own storage SKU: Atlas Cloud Backup Storage for snapshots only, or Atlas Continuous Cloud Backup Storage when continuous backup is enabled in that region. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
Snapshots normally share unchanged data. Deleting one snapshot releases billable unique data only when no retained snapshot still references it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The documented AWS us-east-1 continuous-backup example charges $106.25/month for 115 GB combined storage: 5 GB free, 95 GB at $1.00, and 15 GB at $0.75. This is an illustrative region-specific schedule. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

MongoDB documents disabling and reenabling continuous backup as a way to prevent dual-region billing, but disabling it deletes continuous-backup history. Existing snapshots remain intact; this trade-off sacrifices historical PIT restore coverage. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
Atlas budgets include backup and transfer costs alongside cluster configuration costs; backup is not covered solely by the cluster tier. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Atlas Core Cloud Backups charge retained snapshot storage by provider and storage region. GB-month rates appear as daily GB-days; repeated daily rows do not imply duplicate charges. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Continuous Cloud Backup bills combined snapshot and internal backup-oplog storage using provider-, region-, and usage-tier-dependent rates. Longer restore windows increase retained oplog storage. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Additional-region copies add cross-region transfer and destination storage charges. Copying all backups to one additional region approximately doubles storage quantity; differing regional rates can change the cost ratio. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Atlas stores continuous-backup oplogs in the snapshot region, normally the cluster or shard highest-priority region. Sharded deployments create separate backups for each shard in its primary region. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

After a highest-priority-region change or an oplog-region migration, Atlas temporarily retains and bills backup storage in both regions. It removes old-region data once the new region represents the complete continuous-backup window. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Snapshot storage is incremental where possible. A topology, node, tier, volume, or region change can require another full snapshot and raise retained backup storage. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Copy-region policy items can enable oplog copying for PIT restore after a regional outage. Oplog distribution is configured at the copy-region level, applying to every snapshot copy policy in that region. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

PointFive recommends assigning backup frequency, retention, and regional copies according to environment criticality and recovery needs, then checking existing-snapshot retention updates and compliance-policy minimums before estimating savings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
A Reddit user reported continuous backup at about half their Atlas bill. This is one unverified customer anecdote, not a typical cost share or current pricing benchmark. (low confidence)

OutageDeck archives a MongoDB incident identified and resolved on April 27, 2026: a billing bug inflated some April 24 backup charges without affecting backup configuration, cluster health, or data; MongoDB promised invoice corrections and refunds. (low confidence)
Snapshot copy policies separately specify copy frequency, retention and whether to copy oplogs for PIT recovery in the destination region. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
